title: Golden controller trace (golden_traces/<trace_id>.json)
description: One shared parity case for the fading state machine. The controller exists twice — lua/trace_rt/lib/controller.lua for the runtime and kit/trace_kit/controller.py for the Phase 1 simulator — and a divergence between them silently invalidates Gate G1, because the simulation would certify a controller participants never drive (impl plan section 6). A golden trace is a sequence of per-pass criterion booleans plus the exact event sequence and final state both implementations must produce. The corpus is version-controlled and runs in CI on every change to either side. Impl plan section 3's rule applies: runtime and simulator share no state except controller_config.json and these traces.

description.description: What behaviour this case pins, and why it is in the corpus. Required, not optional: a golden trace whose purpose is not written down becomes unmaintainable the first time it fails.

config_overrides.description: Sections of configs/controller_config.json to shallow-merge before running. Absent for every trace that pins the study configuration; present only where the case IS the deviation (e.g. running with the re-qualification rule off to demonstrate the degenerate machine it prevents).

applicable.description: Corners each element applies to, in a fixed order. An EMPTY list is legal and meaningful: it is the zero-applicable-corners case the impl plan (section 7) requires a defined answer for, where the element is disabled rather than dividing by zero.

criteria.description: The per-pass criterion booleans the controller consumes. null is NO EVIDENCE (the metric was not measurable), not a failure: the pass does not enter that element's evidence window at all.

passes.description: The input stream, in the order passes close.

finish.description: Close the block after the last pass, so elements mid-probe emit their censoring events. Absent when the trace does not exercise block end.

expected_events.description: The exact event sequence, in order. These are fades.schema.json records minus schema_version and block_id, which the runtime stamps and the controller does not know.

expected_disabled_elements.description: Elements with zero applicable corners, in element order.

expected_final_state.description: The controller's full inspectable state after the last pass (and the finish, if any). Compared field for field, so a divergence that happens to emit the same events is still caught.

pinned.description: Reversion cap reached: no further transitions in either direction.

revert_armed.description: False between a reversion and the share's recovery to the revert threshold (one regression, one stage).

corners.description: Each applicable corner's evidence window and consecutive-failure count, in applicable order.
